principles.statement: Human adoption is explicit and never inferred.
Source governance determines eligible inputs; architecture cannot expand source authority.
Every claim preserves class, source lineage, derivation, assumptions, and contamination state.
Thesis implementation and post-thesis extension are always distinguished.
Design-time generation, manufacture, and runtime execution are separate lifecycle stages.
No component authors a rule and adopts that same rule.
No Agent or runtime grants its own permissions.
Knowledge provenance and validation state are first-class.
Evidence records proof but does not create authority.
Runtime may propose but cannot reverse-modify adopted design artifacts.
Railway-domain authority is separate; health and VET-C content do not define MAGP Core.
Unknown or multiply-supported architecture choices remain pending Human decision.
